messages:
sudhir: heads up — customer reported sudden billing spike after last canary swap, looks tied to streaming sessions that fell back mid-request :grimacing:

jess: which customer? any session ids? :eyes:

sudhir: acct AC-772, sample session id `sess_3a7f` in logs. Console provisional line items show ~+1200 tokens in 30s window.

caleb: digging logs now. I see a series of reconnects and toolcall retries where model changed  from `rwd-16g-v2` -> `rwd-8g-compat` mid-stream. Toolcall id `tc-879` repeated 3x. snippet:
```
[2026-02-11T21:00:12Z] req=session=sess_3a7f model=rwd-16g-v2 path=/stream toolcall_id=tc-879 state=handed-off
[2026-02-11T21:00:13Z] fallback=model_mismatch route=alt-region model=rwd-8g-compat toolcall_id=tc-879 retry=1
[2026-02-11T21:00:14Z] client=reconnect toolcall_id=tc-879 payload=... truncated length=1024
```

marco: hmm — our internal toolcall path isn't attaching idempotency keys for streaming handoffs. If a fallback truncates the prefix, the router treats it as a new toolcall and provisional billing emits again. Ledger dedupe kicks in later but console shows the spike to customers immediately.

jess: so impact flow: canary swap -> routing fallback -> truncated prefix -> router creates new toolcall entry -> provisional charge emitted. ledger dedupe marks later but UI shows provisional totals.

caleb: exact. We also see the telemetry tag `prefetch-truncated=true` on those entries. Query: do we want immediate UI smoothing or fix idempotency first?

sudhir: both. quick UI smoothing would reduce customer panic. But we need server-side fix to avoid repeated provisional entries.

marco: proposed server patch (quick sketch):
```
# attach deterministic idempotency for toolcalls across midstream model fallbacks
def toolcall_idempotency_key(session_id, tool_id, payload_prefix):
    if payload_prefix is None: payload_prefix = ''
    return sha256(f"{session_id}:{tool_id}:{payload_prefix}".encode())
```
Then router uses this key when creating provisional ledger entries.
```
``

jess: love it. Edgecase: what about clients that intentionally re-run with different prompt after fallback? We could namespace by `handoff_attempt` but that defeats dedupe for real retries. Need to only dedupe identical prefixes/payloads.

caleb: we can compare `payload_prefix` up to first N tokens. If different, new key -> new charge. If identical, dedupe. N=64 tokens seems reasonable.

billing-bot: FYI — there is a billing alert for AC-772 triggered at 21:02 UTC (provisional spend > $50 in 1m).

deploy-bot: canary deployment rwd-routing-v3 completed at 21:00:05 UTC across us-west-2 and eu-west-1.

marco: next steps I propose:
- short-term: UI smoothing flag that hides provisional spikes for 2m when ledger later confirms dedupe (dashboard PR)
- medium-term: implement deterministic idempotency key based on session+tool+payload_prefix (router + ledger change)
- add an ops alert for model-family-midstream handoffs so we catch regressions

sudhir: ok assign owners — marco for router patch, jess for UI smoothing + dashboard note, caleb for telemetry alert. Put a rollback plan in case canary is the cause.

jess: will open dashboard PR and add a checkbox in console to show "including provisional charges" for now. PR link: https://git.internal/rw/console/pull/4287

caleb: adding alert rule: `midstream_model_handoff_count > 5 per_min per_customer` -> pager on-call.

marco: I have a draft patch, pushing to branch `router/idemp-midstream` — will run unit tests then canary.

sudhir: thanks. let's monitor AC-772 and loop in support so they can proactively message the customer if UI smoothing lands. :thumbsup:
